title.narrative: Lifesaving Nutrition Response in Aweil North and WASH response to populations in Panyijar impacted by multiple crisis

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThe proposed project responds to the critical lifesaving needs of vulnerable populations in Panyijar County (Unity State) and Aweil North County (Northern Bahr el Ghazal State). Concern has selected these counties as they experience above-national average levels of vulnerability to natural disasters, severe food insecurity, inter- and intra-communal conflict, severe malnutrition, and an inflow of returnees and refugees from the Sudan crisis. Further to this, Concern is the nutrition partner in Aweil North with UNICEF and WFP, and there are health service delivery gaps. The presence of significant protection risks, especially gender-based violence, further exacerbates the situation. Concern proposes WASH in Panyijar and Nutrition in Aweil North and will target 27,394 individuals (4,894 men, 7,516 women, 6,953 boys, and 8,032 girls).lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtWASH in Panyijar: ltbrgtConcern proposes a WASH response targeting vulnerable, displaced, and conflict-affected populations in Kol, Nayl Pachar, Ganyiel and Thornhom Payams. This project aims to enhance access to lifesaving WASH services in remote, flood-affected, and conflict-disrupted areas. In consultation with the WASH cluster, RRC, and local administration, Concern will work to improve access to safe water, hygiene, and institutional WASH services, benefiting 18,823 individuals (4,804 men, 5,458 women, 3,953 boys, and 4,518 girls).ltbrgtKey activities include installing two Surface Water Treatment Systems (SWATs), rehabilitating five existing hand pumps, constructing two new hand pumps, and building sanitation facilities in two health centers. Additionally, Concern will promote hygiene practices and provide 500 kits for severely malnourished children (SAM). A further 3,137 WASH kits will be sourced from the core pipeline and transported to Panyijar. Concern will engage 10 community nutrition volunteers (CNVs) to improve the hygiene behaviour and nutrition messaging in the communities. ltbrgtConcern is also conducting a security assessment and deploying local staff familiar with the conflict dynamics. Collaboration with the WASH Directorate, State Ministry of Health, County Health Department (CHD), and Health and Nutrition partners will ensure the integration of WASH interventions for improved nutrition and health outcomes, aligning with WASH cluster objectives. ltbrgtNutrition Aweil North:ltbrgtConcern’s main objective is to increase equitable access and utilization of quality lifesaving nutrition services for children under 5 (CU5) and pregnant and breastfeeding women (PBW) through early detection and treatment of wasting, across four (4) Payams (Ariath, Malual North, Malual East, and Malual Centre Payams). The nutrition services will be delivered to 8,571 (5,571 females and 3,000 males 6,514 CU5 and 2,057 PBW) individuals across five (5) nutrition sites that include Malek Thiep PHCU of Ariath Payam, Rolngut PHCU of Malual North Payam, Mabior Anguai PHCU of Malual East and Pamat PHCU and Kiir Kangbek PHCU of Malual Center. The selection of these sites is due to limited access to nutrition services and large caseloads.ltbrgtThe nutrition program will be implemented through CHD incentive staff using the old CMAM guidelines, with technical support from a nutrition officer and the health and nutrition program manager, under the guidance of the health and nutrition coordinator. This coordinated approach aligns with SSHF 2025 priorities and supports local capacity building. Access to nutrition supplies for treatment and prevention will be facilitated through the core pipeline of UNICEF and WFP. ltbrgtlt/pgt
